research_rationale:
Executive Order 12938 (59 FR 59099, November 16, 1994) declares a national emergency about the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction and their means of delivery, directs export controls, sanctions on foreign persons (Section 4) and on foreign countries (Section 5), and implementation by the Secretaries of State, the Treasury and Commerce. Executive Order 13094 (1998) revised Section 4 and a cross-reference in Section 6, Executive Order 13128 (1999) added subsection 3(e), and Executive Order 13382 (2005) revised Section 4(a); under the strike-and-restate ruling the amended clauses continue. Twenty-nine annual continuation notices are held, the last dated November 5, 2025, which continues the emergency beyond November 14, 2025 and so covers 2026-10-14 (the 2009 notice is not held). The eCFR (amended through 2026-11-06) still carries the Weapons of Mass Destruction Trade Control Regulations citing the order as amended. The inventory was corrected to add the opening declaration of emergency. The order is claimed as in force on 2026-10-14.
Earlier end: Earlier-end test: the order has no own-terms end. The held amendments are Executive Order 13094 (revision of section 4 and a cross-reference in section 6), Executive Order 13128 (new subsection 3(e)) and Executive Order 13382 (revision of section 4(a)); the Office of the Federal Register notes record these as amendments and no revocation. The other held actor texts recite the order or rely on its emergency.
Current basis: Current predicate: the part 539 regulations (31 CFR 539.106 and 539.301 and the authority line, eCFR amended through 2026-11-06) still cite the order as amended by Executive Orders 13094 and 13382, and the nonproliferation statute note to 50 U.S.C. 1701 refers to subsections 4(b) and (c); the bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog found no instrument ending any clause.
